title: Calendar Integration
body:
Things is an outstanding task manager with exceptional design and a highly intuitive structure built around Areas and Projects. It strikes a rare balance between simplicity and depth, making task capture, planning, and review both efficient and enjoyable.

The one notable limitation is the lack of calendar visibility for time-based tasks. Scheduled tasks do not appear in external calendars like Fantastical, Apple Calendar, or Google Calendar, which creates friction for users who rely on time-blocking.

With native calendar integration for scheduled tasks, Things would evolve from an excellent task manager into a complete planning system. Even as it stands, it remains one of the most thoughtfully designed productivity apps available.

title: The Epitome of Simplicity and Productivity
body:
When it comes to organizing my life and staying on top of my tasks, Things 3 has truly been a game-changer. This meticulously designed app has managed to strike the perfect balance between simplicity and functionality, making it an indispensable tool for boosting productivity.

From the moment you open Things 3, its clean and intuitive interface welcomes you with open arms. Creating tasks, setting due dates, and organizing projects have never been easier or more enjoyable. The app’s smooth navigation and seamless integration across all my devices ensure that I never miss a beat, whether I’m on my phone, tablet, or computer.

What truly sets Things 3 apart is its attention to detail. The app understands the importance of focus and provides a clutter-free environment, allowing me to concentrate solely on my tasks. Its powerful features, such as tags, deadlines, and checklists, offer a sense of control and help me prioritize effectively.

Furthermore, Things 3 goes beyond mere task management by incorporating a Today view, which intelligently presents me with the tasks I need to tackle each day. The app’s robust reminder system ensures that deadlines are never missed, keeping me on track and reducing stress.

In summary, Things 3 has revolutionized the way I approach my to-do list. Its minimalist design, seamless synchronization, and thoughtful features have transformed the tedious process of task management into a delightful experience. Whether you’re a busy professional or a meticulous planner, Things 3 is the ultimate companion for taking control of your life.

title: One of the best app ever used.
body:
I just love this application to keep track of the things I have to do at work and home. I have purchased both the iPhone and the Mac App separately and it’s totally worth the money I paid. Though on the expensive side - if you think long term, it kinda works out. 

1. In love with the UI and animations. 
2. The keyboard shortcuts are well thought off. It’s almost like an in-build Apple designed app. 
3. Sync works perfectly well. 
4. Today view with the projects categorically shown. 
5. Scheduling works like a charm, natural language inside the “when” view is very well thought off. You can type 15feb 11 and it will start showing recommendations. 
6. Task repeat feature is also amazing, with both the recurring and the recurring on completion. 
7. Reminders with notifications across all devices. 
8. Integration with Calendars shows all the important events in Today and Upcoming views. 
9. Email to things where you can email your task from your inbox of your choice. 
10. Drag-Drop and multiple window support is very useful for planning your day. 

I think I can go on, but let me end it here so that it doesn’t look like their feature list :P

Kudos to the team at Cultured Code. I am a huge fan now.

author: Asc3ndis

title: Amazing app.
body:
This is a really beautiful piece of software with a few things missing. 

Quick take: TAGS needs major improvements on iOS and iPadOS. Take cues from MacOS please. 

First the good. I am someone who doesn’t stray from the stock iOS apps easily. I will use notes, reminders, calendar, etc by Apple only, since it’s simple and does what I need. But wow, this app is something truly amazing. From the moment you use it the first time, it’s evident that the developers were really passionate about this project and the passion reflect clearly onto the UI of the app. The stock reminders app got a major refresh in iOS 13 and I thought I’d be only using that. But this app is just beyond amazing on the functionality it provides that just can’t be matched with the stock reminders app.   

Obviously, nothing is perfect. There’s always room for improvement. 

Key things needed to further refine this already amazing app: 

1. Allow us to ‘manage’ tags directly. Right now the only way I’ve found to manage/edit tags is to select a current task, and then select the tags menu from it and THEN we are given the option to edit tags. This option should not be hidden under so many lays and should be more easily viewable. Also, the way tags appear at the top of to-do’s on Mac, is really handy. A similar feature on phone and iPad would be nice. 

2. Allow the user to customise the app icon. Quite a few apps have adopted the ‘customisable’ app option allowing the user to choose from various colour pallets. Makes the user like the app more and (at least in my case) I tend to keep it on my home screen rather than hidden in a folder, thus increasing my usage. 

3. (More of a request) Please allow us to rename the “Inbox” tab. Inbox just doesn’t feel right. “To-do” “Reminders” etc etc, if only users had the choice. 🤔

body:
Things has become my daily driver for all my tasks .. anything which comes up to my mind, I type it in the “Inbox”. Today view is a blessing for people like me who dismiss reminders often. The projects section, areas section, heading under each project, all of these are well thought and beautifully laid out. 
Kudos to the CulturedCode team for providing such a wonderful app. 👌🏾👌🏾👌🏾
author: Satish Kumar Perumal

title: Things 3 made me organised
body: Clean, glorious & lightweight features speaks a story how we should organise ourselves into this complex world.

title: Outstandingly clean and clear
body:

If a monthly calendar can be incorporated And if Reminders are not be deleted from Reminders after import u have a winner

title: Great todo app that can be even better
body: Got this app for iOS and the Mac. Been using it for a couple of months now. Really pleased with it. For the asking price however, I think shared lists should really be included. Shared lists would make it a 5-star app for sure.

title: Best To-do App Ever!
body:
Over the years, I've used a lot of To Do apps from plain and simple Reminder to Wunderlist to OmniFocus. Things 3 is the most easiest to use while retaining most of the features that a To Do app needs.

While OmniFocus is featured laden, it's not user-friendly. As for Things 3, I actually look forward to using it every single day!

Kudos to the team behind Things 3!
author: HackNinja

title: Awesome update
body: The good old reliable workhorse is now better than ever. Loving the new headings and checklists features. Keyboard shortcuts for everything!
author: Kranner

title: Definitely worth the wait!
body: I have been using Things since the beginning and have watched it evolve for the better (despite the slow pace). This has the perfect set of features for me - neither too heavy as OmniFocus or too light. The desktop version has some crash bugs which I hope the team will fix soon but this version so far, has been rock-solid. I would definitely recommend this app.
